newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten jettisons usual Easter visit to Britain.
newsitem.headline: Patten jettisons usual Easter visit to Britain.

text.p: The Governor of Hong Kong, Chris Patten, said he would not pay his normal visit to London over the Easter break in March because Britons would be preoccupied with the general election.
"Almost certainly this is the last (visit) that I will pay to the United Kingdom before the general election later this year," Patten said before his departure for London on Wednesday.

Patten is a close friend of British Prime Minister John Major. As the former Conservative party chairman, he was credited with engineering Major's victory in the 1992 polls which cost Patten his own seat.
But the governor sidestepped questions on the timing of the election.
"The next British general election has to be, I think, before about the middle of May," he told a news conference.
"But clearly, people are going to be much preoccupied with that over the Easter period when I would normally have gone to the U.K., so I thought it was sensible to go at this stage."

Patten, the 28th and last British Governor of Hong Kong responsible for steering the colony through its transition to Chinese rule in mid-1997, said he would brief members of both the government and opposition on recent developments.
